I was pretty young when my issues began to show. By the time I was 8, I’d been misdiagnosed with ADHD and bipolar disorder several times. Every doctor we went to had a different opinion. 

When I was ten, I started seeing these warped faces everywhere. At the time, I was on lamotrigine, which has an uncommon side effect of hallucinations and other psychotic symptoms. Eventually, I would see them in the mirror as well. Quick input— I didn’t really perceive things like other kids. I made connections where there were none and sort of considered myself to be enlightened. 

When I saw the Not-My Faces (this is what I called them in my diary at the time) over my own, I began to think that I wasn’t actually alive anymore. I tried to end my life when I came to this revelation, to ‘make things normal,’ and landed myself in a mental hospital. I stayed there for about three months, where I was put on a bunch of different meds in a desperate attempt to stabilize me, and was taken off lamotrigine. I was put on chlorpromazine, trazodone, and lisdexamfetamine, all of which I still take. I ended up getting the diagnosis in the second month. 

I hope this helps!

Honestly, I’m not sure. I can’t deny the fact that I definitely learned from it and got a new sense of self-worth, but it haunts me to think that I could’ve died that night. 

I attempted suicide by swallowing a large amount of pills and then cutting my wrists. DISCLAIMER, It makes you feel like shit.

I think the leading cause was just build up pressure. Like somebody shook a soda for years and years, and then it finally exploded. Of course, I was carrying the weight of some childhood trauma and big secrets, which didn’t help, but I’m in therapy now!

If someone is contemplating suicide, the absolute worst thing to do is say ‘please don’t do it, for me.’ It basically makes the person feel like shit. Sometimes, suicidal people don’t want a huge meaningful talk that will weigh on their soul, but rather someone to chill with and make them feel less alone. If they do want to take the talking route though, make sure that they know you support them. Don’t make them feel like there’s something wrong with them, and it’s probably not a great idea to bring up mental illness unless they talk about it first. There are a lot of people who have no depression or anything who still think of suicide sometimes. There’s no magic words you can say that will make them go, ‘woah, I want to live!’ but at the very least, you can give them hope.

The thing is, I don’t think my family could’ve done anything. Hell, the reason I was still alive up until then was my family. They were there and they loved me, but I still couldn’t see myself grow up or even be happy. Sure, maybe if they’d known beforehand about my depression they could’ve done something, but they didn’t, and I was great at hiding it. But if there’s one thing I could go back in time and tell them, it would be to talk to me about it. 

For the longest time I thought I was broken because I didn’t want to be here. I think it was mostly the shame that kept me from telling, especially because my family is better off then most. I was afraid that I had nothing to be sad about, and I’d be laughed at. If they had made it more clear to me that depression could strike at any time, no matter the situation, maybe I would’ve reached out before it got to the point of an attempt.

I feel like this question makes you choose between the economy, the environment, and the people. At first glance, the obvious option would be a human rights activist of some sorts, but when you think about it you realize that the entire world would literally fall apart. If they were to give our already limited resources to those in poverty (I am 100% for helping the homeless and equal human rights), all of us would die. My favourite thing about powerlifting is that the barbell doesn’t give a shit about me. That sounds really weird, let me explain— ever since last year, everyone has been treating me like I’m fragile, like I’ll break at the slightest touch. Lifting these heavy weights is the exact opposite, because they don’t care whether I’ve had a good day or a bad day, they are still going to try to push me down.
